name: Sung Sot Cave
kicker: The wide cave on the long boat
summary: The widest cave on the long boat: climb the steep path and walk the chambers on a 5–6 hour route. A freshwater lake is in the first chamber, and a stalagmite like Quan Âm is in the last. The landing is on the Bồ Hòn line, 20 m above the sea. Thiên Cung, on the short boat, uses that same height. Take the long route when this cave is the point.
getThere: Route 2 boat from the Ha Long passenger port
heroCaption: The lit chamber, with the crowd small under the ceiling

notice.title: 20 metres is also Thien Cung
notice.body: The port puts Sửng Sốt 20 m above the sea, and puts Thiên Cung 20 m above the sea on the other route. Both figures stay. The path here is steep.

body: The landing is on the Bồ Hòn line. You climb into the chamber called the widest yet found on the bay. A freshwater lake is in the first chamber. A stalagmite like Quan Âm is in the last. The path is steep.

The clock is route 2, 5–6 hours for Ti Tốp, Sửng Sốt, and Luồn together. Thiên Cung, on route 1, is also 20 m above the sea. Bring an identity card or a passport. From 10 December 2025 a bay ticket needs one.

figures.caption: Another chamber on the same visit, with the crowd under the formations
figures.alt: Visitors in a chamber of Sung Sot Cave, Ha Long Bay

gettingThere: Route 2 from Cảng tàu khách quốc tế Hạ Long. The English port line is Beach road, New Beach, Bai Chay ward, 500 m from Sun World. The route is 5–6 hours for Ti Tốp, Sửng Sốt, and Luồn together.

legs.heading: From the Ha Long port
legs.body: The route-2 boat. The clock is the whole 5–6 hour route for Ti Tốp, Sửng Sốt, and Luồn together.

closed: No weekly closing day was printed. Confirm the sailing the day you go.
admissionNote: No separate cave price. Route 2 on 15 March 2024 is 490,000–510,000 đồng, split there as 310,000 sightseeing and 200,000 boat. The port fee in that notice is 40,000–60,000 đồng, and 60,000 of the 310,000 is the port fee. That notice takes 20 percent off for children 7 to 15. The board exemption page, updated 2 November 2024, takes 20 percent off from age 7 to under 16, and gives free entry under 1.2 m or under 7. From 10 December 2025 a bay ticket needs an identity card or a passport.
